newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Drugs drive Swedish sharemarket to a new high.
newsitem.headline: Drugs drive Swedish sharemarket to a new high.

text.p: Sweden's sharemarket closed at a new high on Monday, opening higher in line with gains in New York and boosted during the day by rising drug stocks.
The general index closed 0.62 percent higher at 2,932.80. Shares totalling 5.44 billion crowns changed owners.
The drugs sector index rose 1.81 percent with drugs major Astra rising 2.5 crowns to 139.5 amid expectations of imminent FDA approval for its asthma Pulmicort Turbuhaler.
Brokers were mixed on whether or not the share would continue climbing.
"An FDA approval of Pulmicort will not necessarily lift the share significantly," one broker said.
Fellow drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn gained five to 266.5 crowns.
Gains by telecoms company and index heavyweight Ericsson also underpinned the index. The share ended up 2.5 crowns at 292, but off highs. Institutional investors were buying the share, brokers said.
Rollerbearings maker SKF ended up seven crowns at 208.5 on a rumour that a Stockholm brokerage had placed a buy recommendation on the share.
Shares in forestry company MoDo jumped 12 crowns to 259 while the forestry sector index sagged 0.59 percent.
"All forestry companies, except MoDo, rose sharply on Thursday. They are playing catch-up today," said Karl-Johan Krigstrom, forestry analyst at Enskilda Securities.
